findings.reason: without the acquiring call named, the repair and its negative control target a mechanism the station may never invoke, so the node would either find nothing to change or change the wrong file, and its control could not be written.
findings.text: §48 gives two hypotheses for how the station holds a pointer lock (a `with _pointer_lock(...)` enclosing the tick's loop, or a generator suspended inside one), but neither has a caller in the code the plan cites: `_pointer_lock` is acquired only in `reckon/crew/runs.py` (`_mutate_pointer` at 464, dispatch requeue at 885 and 942, stacking at 1729) and in `reckon/crew/queue_admission.py` (pass-side relaunch/writeback at 343, 1761 and 1822), while `station.py`, `station_subscriber.py` and `obligations.py` contain no acquisition and call only reads (`runs.list_live`/`read_pointer`/`drain`/`run_acknowledgement`, `queue_admission.queued_placements`/`recorded_pass_hold`). The plan's own stack samples showed no `_pointer_lock` frame, and no `with _pointer_lock` exists in `station.py` at all, so the first hypothesis is falsified by the file, and the second requires an acquisition nothing in the station performs. A plan that pre-commits the repair ("the station takes a run's pointer lock only around the read-modify-write it protects") on a mechanism with no reachable caller sends the node at a code path that may not exist, while the cited evidence fits a cause the plan does not consider — an inherited descriptor in a forked child, or an fd leaked by a caller outside the station's own modules.

findings.text: §48 is declared `implementable` with `reckon/crew/obligations.py` among its write paths, and §45 (line 301) is also `implementable` with `reckon/crew/obligations.py` among its write paths, yet `plan-section-depends-on` carries no `s48` key and no entry links the two. Two implementable sections editing one file with no declared order are dispatched together by a coordinator following the map, giving two worktrees editing the same module and a merge the plan never ordered.

The plan-state contract requires the chain to close visibly with an open followup carrying the next one-line invocation; as written a resumed coordinator is pointed at finished work and the newly added section is reachable from no invocation.

findings.reason: the stated repair and its control both depend on that attribution, so an ungated investigation lets an implausible attribution survive into the change it is supposed to justify.
findings.text: the deliverable's first half ("The worker reproduces the station's tick against a temporary crew home holding a delivered review run, records which call acquires that run's pointer lock and how long it is held, and names the enclosing frame or the unclosed generator") is measured by nothing in the done-when: the cases assert only that no pointer lock is held after a tick and that an acquisition returns within one second, and the attribution is required only to appear in the manifest. A worker can pass both while recording a guessed attribution, and no negative control can fail on a wrong attribution.

findings.reason: the control's expected outcome has to be a bounded wait whose timeout is the red signal, otherwise the node can neither report a clean control nor tell a hang from a pass.
findings.text: the negative control reads "restoring the lock-holding call makes that acquisition wait for the tick", which presumes the restored defect releases the lock when the tick ends. The plan's own second hypothesis is an unclosed generator suspended inside a pointer-lock block; if that is what the investigation names, the restored defect holds the lock for the life of the station, so the acquisition never loses the race and "wait for the tick" never ends — the control hangs, or trips a suite-wide timeout, instead of turning one case red.
